wave: CENSUS BLINDNESS -- 8 of 60 donors in `.atlas/references/donor-corpus.toml` carried a `decision_status` of the literal placeholder `"PENDING"` even though their own `census_status` already showed a completed (or lane-level-concluded) census, with a real, dated, per-mechanism disposition already recorded in each donor's own census document (and, for 5 of the 8, in a shared lane synthesis document's own explicit `## Decision` section). The machine-readable decision_status field was never synced to the decision the prose had already reached -- one donor's own census doc (duumbi.md) explicitly names the missing step: 'A coordinator must merge applicable Discoveries/target_owners into ... donor-corpus.toml separately.' That merge was never done for any of the 8.
wave_title: Thirty-first generation this cycle. Checked the absorption/extinction overlay first (per the standing directive): no donor is currently census-sufficient with a genuinely open ABSORB_NOW/REJECT/DEFER question, so this generation instead closes the most valuable gap surfaced by that same check -- 8 donors whose already-resolved decision was never mirrored into the machine-readable tracker, exactly the kind of undetectable staleness the standing loop's own priority order names as 'census blindness.'
priority_classification: census blindness -- the repository's own machine-readable self-model (donor-corpus.toml) silently disagreed with its own prose evidence (census docs, a lane synthesis doc) for 8 donors, in a way no prior test or generation ever checked. Selected ahead of a fresh correctness survey because a knowledge-integrity gap that makes the system's own state self-contradictory is a stronger violation of architectural integrity than an unverified new code path, and this gap was directly discoverable from the donor-corpus census-depth-vs-decision cross-tabulation the absorption/extinction overlay check already requires running every generation.
gap_discovered_by: Running this generation's mandatory absorption/extinction overlay check: cross-tabulating every donor's (census_status, decision_status) pair in donor-corpus.toml by hand (python3 one-liner) to look for a donor whose census is sufficient but decision_status is still PENDING -- the exact state the user's earlier directive requires never be left unclassified. Found 8 such donors (iris, sigil-lang, duumbi, composer, clef, egglog, wasm-component-model, wasm-spec), then independently verified each by reading its own census document's '## Census State' section AND, for the 5 semantic-graph-language-lane donors, the lane synthesis document's own '## Decision' section directly -- confirming in every case that a real decision (REFERENCE_ONLY / ABSORB_LATER / REJECT / EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY per mechanism, zero ABSORB_NOW anywhere) was already reached and dated, not merely that census activity had occurred.
key_finding: duumbi.md's own '## Census State' section explicitly states: 'A coordinator must merge applicable Discoveries/target_owners into `.atlas/provenance/donors/donor-clone-index.json`, `.atlas/roadmap/DONOR-ABSORPTION-PLAN.toml`, and `.atlas/references/donor-corpus.toml` separately' -- proving this sync step was anticipated as necessary by the census-writing generation itself, but never completed by any subsequent generation. The semantic-graph-language-lane synthesis document (.atlas/census/donors/semantic-graph-language-lane-2026-09-22.md) reaches an explicit, dated '## Decision' verdict covering all 5 of its member donors (iris, sigil-lang, duumbi, composer, clef): 'Zero mechanisms across all five donors met the evidence bar for ABSORB_NOW,' with per-mechanism REFERENCE_ONLY/ABSORB_LATER/REJECT/EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY dispositions already tabulated -- yet all 5 donor-corpus.toml entries still read decision_status = "PENDING", the literal 'nobody has looked at this yet' placeholder. Identical pattern for egglog/wasm-component-model/wasm-spec: each has its own complete '## Disposition (per concept)' table (all STUDY/ADAPT/DEFER/REJECT, matching their already-correct runtime_dependency_status = "NOT_ADOPTED_AS_RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY"), but decision_status was never updated to match.
verification_before_acting: Ran a python3 cross-tabulation of every donor's (census_status, decision_status) pair directly against the real donor-corpus.toml text, finding 8 donors at a census depth beyond SKELETON/PENDING_DEEP_CENSUS with decision_status still literally PENDING (the remaining 13 PENDING entries are all honestly SKELETON, correctly excluded).

Read all 8 donors' full donor-corpus.toml entries directly, confirming native_replacement and runtime_dependency_status were ALREADY accurate/resolved for every one of them -- only decision_status itself was stale, ruling out a broader multi-field drift.

Read duumbi.md, composer.md, clef.md, iris.md, and sigil-lang.md's own '## Census State' sections directly, plus the full semantic-graph-language-lane-2026-09-22.md synthesis document end to end (its Provenance flags, Mechanism comparison, Discoveries table, Blueprint Revision Candidates section, and its own '## Decision' section) -- confirming a real, already-reached, cross-donor decision exists for all 5 lane members, not merely raw census activity.

Read egglog.md, wasm-component-model.md, and wasm-spec.md's own '## Disposition (per concept)' tables and '## Census State' sections directly, confirming each independently reached a complete, resolved (all-STUDY/ADAPT/DEFER/REJECT, zero ABSORB_NOW) per-concept verdict.

Checked for an existing Rust test enforcing any relationship between census_status and decision_status before writing a new one -- confirmed none existed (grepped for both field names across every .rs file in the workspace: zero hits outside this generation's own new parser fields).

design_decisions.question: What decision_status string to write for the 8 corrected donors, given the field has no code-enforced enum (pure freeform TOML)?
design_decisions.decision: Reused this file's own existing STUDY_FOR_<LANE>_LANE naming convention (already used by capndonor entries capnproto/rkyv/agentir as STUDY_FOR_BINARY_FORMAT_LANE / STUDY_FOR_BINARY_FORMAT_LANE_CONDITIONAL_CACHE_DEPENDENCY / STUDY_FOR_PIPELINE_STAGING_DISCIPLINE) rather than inventing a new vocabulary: STUDY_FOR_SEMANTIC_GRAPH_LANGUAGE_LANE for the 5 lane donors (iris, sigil-lang, duumbi, composer, clef), STUDY_FOR_DECISION_LAYER_LANE for egglog, STUDY_FOR_INTERFACE_BOUNDARY_LANE for wasm-component-model, STUDY_FOR_VERIFY_THEN_ENCODE_LANE for wasm-spec -- each name drawn directly from that donor's own census doc's stated 'donor gap' scope phrase, not invented from scratch.

design_decisions.question: Should composer's decision_status be the bare 'ABSORB_LATER' instead, since 2 of its discovered mechanisms (thin-middle-end doctrine, PHG/hyperedges) did get an ABSORB_LATER disposition in the lane synthesis?
design_decisions.decision: No. The 4 donors that already carry a bare 'ABSORB_LATER' decision_status in this file (buck2, datafrog, differential-dataflow, salsa) are cases where the WHOLE donor is a single absorption target for a later wave -- a materially different claim than 'most of this donor's mechanisms were rejected or filed reference-only; two specific sub-mechanisms are worth revisiting later.' Using bare ABSORB_LATER for composer would overclaim a whole-donor absorption intent the lane synthesis explicitly does not make; STUDY_FOR_<LANE>_LANE accurately summarizes 'studied, mixed per-mechanism dispositions recorded, see evidence for specifics' without conflating the two shapes of claim.

design_decisions.question: Should this generation also correct census_status for iris/sigil-lang (still DEEP_CENSUS_ACTIVE, not fully complete per their own docs -- execution-based verification and full transitive-crate reads remain undone)?
design_decisions.decision: No. Their own census docs are explicit that DEEP_CENSUS_ACTIVE for them means the REQUESTED mechanism set is source-verified and complete, with only broader (not currently blocking) follow-up work named -- that is an honest, accurate census_status, not a stale one. Only decision_status was actually wrong (claiming no decision existed when the lane synthesis document had already reached one at this exact census depth). Changing census_status itself was out of scope and not evidenced as wrong.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every donor in donor-corpus.toml whose decision_status reads the literal placeholder "PENDING" now has a census_status honestly showing that no decision could yet exist (SKELETON or PENDING_DEEP_CENSUS); the 8 donors whose census was already sufficient for a real, already-recorded decision now carry that decision in decision_status, not a stale placeholder. This invariant is now permanently, automatically enforced.

Only then were the 8 decision_status values corrected, and the test re-run to confirm it now passes.
